transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, I came in because... ever since my wife’s fall, things have just completely derailed for me. 

I’ve always been the man with the lists and the plan, you know? The one who keeps everything organized. But lately, I just find myself sitting at the kitchen table staring at her medication chart. I'll start crying out of nowhere, or I'll snap over absolutely nothing. And I'm just letting everything else go. The bills, my mentoring calls, even basic housework—it's all just piling up. It's like I just can’t make myself function anymore.
Did your wife die after the fall?

No, no, she didn't pass away. But... well, there hasn't really been an end to the situation yet. 

She survived, but she was left with serious mobility problems. The caregiving demands are just a constant part of every single day for me now. So all of this—me falling apart, the stress—it's all been happening while the situation is still very much ongoing. There really isn't a break from it.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

No, I wouldn't say it's all day, every day. It's more like... I just get these sudden waves where it hits me, and that's when I start crying or feeling completely overwhelmed. But I don't feel depressed from the moment I wake up until I go to sleep. It just comes and goes depending on what I'm trying to deal with at the moment.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say that. I still care about the things I usually like. If I actually get a minute to sit down and read, or if I put a baseball game on the TV, I still enjoy it. 

It's just... I rarely have the time or the mental energy to actually do any of those things right now. But the interest itself hasn't gone away.
Have these symptoms made it hard for you to handle your usual responsibilities?

Yes, they really have. I mean... I've stopped showing up for my mentoring and community commitments. I just can't manage them right now. And even the basics around the house—things I used to handle without even thinking about it, like paying the bills, keeping the house up, just normal household routines—they're all slipping badly.
Have you been feeling especially anxious or on edge?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I feel anxious or nervous. Like I mentioned, I just feel completely overwhelmed by everything I'm trying to deal with right now, but it's not really an edgy or panicky feeling. I'm just... bogged down by it all.
Have you been feeling hopeless?

No, I wouldn't say hopeless. I don't feel like things will never get better or anything like that. It's really just the weight of everything right now. I just feel like I'm drowning in it all at the moment, but I don't feel like there's no hope.
Have you been doing things lately that are out of character for you or that break important rules or responsibilities?

No, nothing like that. I mean, besides what I already mentioned about letting the bills and my mentoring slide. That's certainly out of character for me, because I've always been a very responsible person. But as far as breaking important rules or... doing something reckless, no. I'm just having a hard time keeping up, that's all. I haven't been acting out or anything.
Have you been getting unusually irritable or angry lately?

Yes, actually. I have been snapping over nothing, really. It's a big part of why I came in. Ever since my wife’s fall, I’ve gone from being the man with the lists and the plan to just... sitting at the kitchen table staring at her medication chart. I'll find myself crying or just snapping at her over the smallest things. And like I mentioned before, I'm letting the bills and my mentoring calls slide, but it's also basic housework piling up now, too. It's like I just can’t make myself function.
Have you become physically aggressive with anyone since your wife’s fall?

No, absolutely not. I mean, I know I said I've been snapping at her, but it's strictly verbal. I haven't been physically aggressive with anyone. I would never do that. It's just... I get overwhelmed and frustrated, but no, no violence or anything like that.
Besides feeling overwhelmed, have you been feeling sad?

I don't know if I'd call it sad, exactly. I mean, I know I just said I find myself crying, but... that really feels like it's just from the frustration of it all. It's not like a deep sadness or feeling down in the dumps, if that's what you mean. It's mostly just that I'm so completely overwhelmed with her care and everything else piling up, and I just kind of hit a wall.
Since your wife’s fall, have you been doing anything that would count as serious misbehavior or breaking rules?

No, no, nothing like that. I'm not... I haven't been getting into any trouble or breaking any rules. I'm just sitting at home trying to manage her care and failing at it. But no, no bad behavior or anything like you're talking about.
Since your wife’s fall, have you been feeling depressed?

No, I wouldn't say depressed. Like I said about feeling sad, it's really just the stress of the whole situation. I don't feel empty or hopeless like I think depression is supposed to feel. I'm just incredibly stressed out and, you know, struggling to keep my head above water with all the caregiving. But no, not depressed.
Since your wife’s fall, have you done anything that seriously violated other people’s rights or major social rules?

No, absolutely not. I haven't done anything like that. I'm just trying to get through the days and take care of my wife. I don't have the time or energy to be causing trouble or bothering anyone else, let alone violating anyone's rights.
Since your wife’s fall, have you had a depressed mood?
No, I... I think we just covered that. I don't feel depressed, just completely overwhelmed by having to do everything for her now. It's just stress.
Since your wife’s fall, have you been crying a lot?

Yes, actually, I have. That is a big part of why I came in. I've always been the man with the lists and the plan, you know? But since her fall, I'll just find myself sitting at the kitchen table, staring at her medication chart, and I just start crying. Or I'll snap over absolutely nothing. 

It's like I just can't make myself function right now. I'm letting the bills pile up, I'm missing my mentoring calls, and even basic housework is just sitting there untouched. So... yes, I have been crying a lot more than I'd like to admit.
When you start crying, do you also feel down or low inside?

No, I wouldn't say I feel low or down. Like I mentioned a minute ago, it's not really a sadness thing. It's more that I just feel... completely overwhelmed by everything I have to manage now. The tears just sort of happen because it's all too much, not because I'm feeling down inside.
When you cry, do you feel sad?

I... well, I feel like I just answered that. No, I don't feel sad. Like I said a second ago, it really isn't a sadness thing. I'm just completely overwhelmed by the sheer amount of responsibility on my shoulders right now. The crying is just from the stress of it all being too much, not because I'm sad.
